Sexual crimes at the Oktoberfest doubles despite poor attendance and increased police presence (Translation in the comments)

Sexual harassment has always been a topic during the Oktoberfest. However, it's a especial focus this year due to the happenings in Cologne. The police of Munich makes a statement after the first week.

It is the second days of Wiesn (col. Oktoberferst). A young Swiss girl is attending the Oktoberfest with her girlfriend for the first time. Even though it's raining, they're having a fun day. They met nice people in the tents, drank a couple liters of bier and shared a pork knuckle.

Suddenly, she feels a hand on her hip, then on her butt. She turns around, behind her stands a man smiling. She tells him he should stop that. He ignores her, pulls her tightly against him and tries to kiss her. He only let her go after she kicks him.

It could have happened like that. Sure is that the Swiss girl was harassed. And the sad thing is that she isn't the only one with such experiences in the biggest fair of the world. According to the police there have been 16 sexual crimes so during the first week of the Oktoberfest. This includes sexual acts and also sexual-based insults with and without physical interaction. "Thanks god there haven't been any reports about rape", says Werner Feiler, vice-president of Munich's police. An attempted rape occured already on the first day, though.

The big wave of harassment didn't occur

After the incidents of new year's eve, many were very afraid that something similar could happen in a big celebration such as the Oktoberfest. Right-wingers predicted a wave of dancing pickpocketers at the Wiesn.

However, these fears didn't materialize. The police speaker Marcus da Gloria Martins explains that there are no indications of something similar to Cologne happening in Munich. The suspects are also very international, many of them being Germans. Only 6 of them are refugees.

Twice as many sexual crimes as in 2015

Nevertheless, the increase in sexual crime is alarming. In 2015 there were 8 sexual crimes during the first week, and seven in 2014. "This increase can be explained by the fact that many of our officers are disguised as civilians and act proactively when there is something going on", says Feiler. The reporting of the crime is similar to the past years.

Since 2003 there is the initiative "Safy Wiesn for girls and women". Anyone needing help of counseling can visit the Security Point of the initiative direct at the Red Cross. In spite of the reduction in the number of people attending the Oktoberfest, the number of people looking for help at the Security Point has stayed the same, says Kristina Gottlöber, speaker of the initiative to FOCUS.

"Most of the time are women who can't find their friends or hotel", adds Gottlöber. Also because of sexual violence. Gottlöber couldn't say any precise number. Last year, 196 women were counseled.

Many victims don't file any reporting

"It's surprising that women often do not realize that someone is touching them", says Gloria Martins. Women have been groped for years. It's unclear how big the number of unreported cases is. Most of the time no report is filed.
